note.question: Can a truckload procurement market use compact bids to allocate bundles efficiently while producing simple, anonymous, budget-balanced prices that carriers and shippers can interpret?
note.overview: Carriers submit combinatorial procurement bids and the mechanism jointly determines efficient allocations and anonymous linear prices. The paper proves conditions for individual rationality, budget balance, and exact or approximate Walrasian equilibrium.

models.name: Integrated winner determination and anonymous lane pricing for combinatorial truckload procurement auctions and exchanges
models.summary: Carriers submit combinatorial procurement bids and the mechanism jointly determines efficient allocations and anonymous linear prices. The paper proves conditions for individual rationality, budget balance, and exact or approximate Walrasian equilibrium.
objects: A shipper or shipper conglomerate procuring coverage for lanes
Multiple carriers that submit package or compact network bids and may exchange lane obligations
inputs: Carriers privately know their networks, existing contracts, operational constraints, and lane-covering costs
The baseline compact-bidding benchmark assumes disclosure of network information to a trusted auctioneer
The experiments also vary partial disclosure and quantify the efficiency cost of withholding private network information
The auctioneer observes submitted bids but does not require full enumeration of all possible packages
decisions: Carriers report package costs or compact network and lane-cost information
Under the exchange format, carriers may buy and sell existing lane obligations
The shipper procures the required lane coverage under the allocation and anonymous-pricing rules
assumptions: Carrier and shipper payoffs are quasilinear in money
Every required lane is covered either by a carrier or through an exogenous-cost spot-market option
The shipper is a net procurer; carriers bring truck capacity and, in the exchange, tradable existing obligations
Compact bids encode lane and empty-movement costs with a polynomial number of parameters
Exact Walrasian prices require no integer-program relaxation gap; the general construction allows epsilon-Walrasian prices and residual envy

components.label: Exact or epsilon-Walrasian equilibrium with anonymous linear lane prices
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Exact or epsilon-Walrasian equilibrium with anonymous linear lane prices. Proposition 1 establishes individual rationality and Walrasian equilibrium from the dual when there is no relaxation gap. Proposition 5 shows that the terminating iterative dual-pricing mechanism is individually rational, strongly budget balanced, and Walrasian under the same condition; Section 3.5 extends the construction to epsilon-Walrasian prices.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Carriers submit bids describing costs and feasible lane bundles. The auctioneer first solves the winner-determination problem. It then runs iterative dual pricing: a winner-aware dual proposes lane prices, carrier-specific separation problems identify preferred nonwinning packages, and violated Walrasian constraints are added until none remains. Final lane prices determine carrier and shipper payments.
